issues.description: The problem statement and the template's example use animal constructors that take only a name (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")), and the UML shows Animal has only a name attribute. The solution implementation introduces an additional age attribute and constructors requiring (String name, int age) for Animal and all subclasses. This constructor signature mismatch can confuse students and prevent them from following the provided Main example or the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the constructor design across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement, UML, and template Main to specify an age attribute and show constructors accepting (String name, int age), or (B) modify the solution to remove the age attribute and provide constructors that accept only a single String name (and adjust subclasses accordingly). This will ensure the UML, example usage in Main, template, and solution use the same constructor signatures.

issues.description: Constructor signatures for Animal-derived classes are inconsistent across artifacts: the template Main.java (and the problem description examples) create Seal/Pig/Goat with a single String parameter (name), while the solution's Animal class defines a constructor requiring (String name, int age) and the concrete classes' constructors also take an age parameter. This mismatch in constructor parameters (and the implicit additional 'age' attribute in the solution) breaks the direct mapping between the problem/template examples and the provided solution, likely confusing students about the expected class attributes and constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent across problem, template, and solution. Either: (A) Remove the extra 'age' attribute from the solution's Animal and change its constructor (and concrete classes) to accept only String name to match the problem/template examples; or (B) Update the problem statement and template Main.java examples to document and use the two-argument constructors (String name, int age) and mention the 'age' attribute so students and the solution align.
